blocks.text: The Bharat Scouts & Guides (BS&G)
Overview

The Bharat Scouts & Guides (BS&G) is the national Scouting and Guiding association of India. Registered under the Societies Registration Act, BS&G operates as a non-political, non-sectarian, and non-communal organization. Scouting was introduced in India in 1909, followed by Guiding in 1911. The organization is structured in a hierarchy of local, district, and state associations, with the President of India serving as Chief Patron and the Vice-President of India as Patron. Regular training and reorientation programmes are conducted for Scouts, Guides, and their leaders. Scouting / Guiding is an approved method of character building for good citizenship aimed at developing leadership qualities and promoting self-control, self-reliance, and self-direction.
Mission and Vision
Mission: To contribute to the education of young people through a value system based on the Scout Promise and Law.
Vision: To be a globally recognized, consistently growing, self-reliant youth movement that is gender-balanced, vibrant, and responsive to trends.
Principles
Duty to God: Adherence to spiritual principles and loyalty to one's religion.
Duty to Others: Loyalty to one's country, fostering peace, understanding, cooperation, and societal development.
Duty to Self: Responsibility for one's own development.

Service
Promise
"On my honour, I promise that I will do my best – to do my duty to God and my country, to help other people, and to obey the Scout/Guide Law."

SKILL DEVELOPMENT CENTER -SDC

Purposeful, growth-oriented, and productive education is essential in today’s competitive environment. Corporations are on the lookout for dynamic, result-oriented, and enterprising individuals capable of independently handling various challenges and making informed decisions. While university degrees are essential, they only take students to the interview stage. The defining factor that helps candidates secure positions and succeed within companies is their skill set.

To meet the needs of the modern corporate world, it is crucial to integrate industry-specific skill requirements with the college curriculum, creating a sustainable platform for these initiatives. The Skill Development Centre (SDC) at Dr. Lankapalli Bullayya College was established in 2011 to address the training needs of students across various undergraduate programs (B. A., B. Com., B. Sc, BBM) and engineering disciplines (Computer Science Engineering, Electronics and Communication Engineering, Civil Engineering, Electrical and Electronics Engineering). It also serves postgraduate programs including MBA, MCA, M. A., and M. Sc. courses.

To enhance the efforts of the SDC, the college has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with NASSCOM for the Global Business Foundation Programme, which trains students through their ‘Train the Trainer’ program. NASSCOM, the National Association of Software and Services Companies, is a non-profit global trade body with over 1,500 members, including companies from the United States, UK, EU, Japan, and China. NASSCOM’s member companies are involved in software development, software services, software products, IT-enabled/BPO services, and e-commerce.

The SDC is a progressive and student-friendly initiative of the Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) and collaborates closely with the Career Guidance and Placements Cell (CG&PC). Its primary objective is to bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and the practical realities of the global job market. The centre boasts a dynamic, well-structured syllabus that is periodically revised to keep pace with changing times. It conducts sessions on personality development, communication skills, group discussions, and kinesics, adopting a holistic approach to training and development. This comprehensive and result-oriented training has successfully placed many students in reputable companies.

Institution’s Innovation Council (IIC)

The Institution’s Innovation Council (IIC) of Dr. Lankapalli Bullayya College, Visakhapatnam, is established under the AICTE Innovation Cell to promote innovation, entrepreneurship, and research culture within the institution. IIC provides a structured platform for students and faculty to develop innovative ideas, participate in design thinking activities, file patents, and transform projects into start-ups. It regularly conducts workshops, hackathons, IPR awareness programs, industry interaction sessions, and entrepreneurship development activities as per AICTE guidelines. IIC strengthens the institutional ecosystem, enhances research output, and contributes to the development of an entrepreneurial mindset among students through systematic planning and implementation of innovation-driven initiatives.
Vision of IIC

To build a vibrant innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystem that nurtures creativity, research excellence, intellectual property generation, and start-up culture among students and faculty, thereby contributing to technological advancement and national development.
Mission of IIC
To systematically promote innovation, ideation, and design thinking practices in the institution.
To encourage start-up incubation, product development, and commercialization of research outcomes.
To strengthen industry–institute collaboration for real-time problem solving.
To promote IPR awareness and increase patent filing and research publications.
Functions of IIC Committee
Prepare and implement annual innovation activity calendar as per AICTE guidelines.
Organize workshops, seminars, hackathons, impact lectures, and start-up awareness programs.
Identify and mentor student innovators and entrepreneurial teams.
Facilitate patent filing, copyright registration, and IPR activities.
Coordinate with incubators, industries, MSMEs, and financial institutions.
Monitor and document innovation-related activities for AICTE IIC reporting.
Support participation in national innovation contests and rankings such as ARIIA.
Review progress periodically and recommend improvement strategies.
Profile

Dr. Lankapalli Bullayya College was established in 1973, initially offering a three-year Bachelor of Commerce degree programme. The college was sanctioned government aid in 1976. By 1988, it had expanded to include courses in the Arts, Science, and Commerce departments. Currently, the college offers Honours undergraduate courses in four different disciplines. All courses are of four-year duration and follow a semester pattern in accordance with the guidelines of Andhra University. The conduct of semester-end theory and practical examinations, as well as the issuance of degrees, is the prerogative of Andhra University.
The undergraduate program is divided into two divisions for academic functions:
1. Commerce & Management: B. Com. and BBA
2. Arts & Sciences: B. Sc. and B. A.
Admission criteria
Admissions are conducted through the Online Admissions Module for Degree Colleges (OAMDC) under the Andhra Pradesh State Council of Higher Education (APSCHE).
UG Courses

The college offers a diverse range of undergraduate programmes, including Bachelor of Science (B.Sc. Hon. ) with ten major subjects and Bachelor of Arts (B.A. Hon. ) with six major subjects. In addition to these, the college also provides courses in Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA Hon. ) and Bachelor of Commerce (B.Com. Hon. ), catering to a variety of academic interests and career aspirations.

A dedicated Placement Cell in collaboration with SDC assists students with career guidance and placements. It organises placement drives over the academic year inviting top companies and various industries and also provides essential skill development training for on-campus recruitments. The college environment fosters students' overall development and growth by encouraging participation in both academics and co-curricular and extracurricular activities.
PROFILE

The Post Graduate courses at Dr. Lankapalli Bullayya College were launched in 1993 with the introduction of the Master of Arts and Master of Science programs in Mathematics. In 1994, the MBA and MCA programs were introduced, each with an intake of 30 students per course. At present, the college has 10 departments offering 12 courses, all affiliated to Andhra University. These courses are career-oriented and inspire students to pursue higher education through Master's programs.

Any science graduate who has secured a qualifying rank in the APPGCET (Common Entrance Test conducted by the Government of Andhra Pradesh) is eligible to pursue these courses.
Graduates who secured a qualifying rank in the APPGCET from Arts and Commerce streams are eligible to pursue postgraduate courses in English and Commerce, respectively.

SERVICES OFFERED

Placement Cell: A dedicated Placement Cell assists students with career guidance and placements, providing essential skill development training to prepare them for on-campus recruitment opportunities. The college fosters an environment that supports students' overall development by encouraging active participation not only in academics but also in co-curricular and extracurricular activities.
Infrastructure: The well-planned infrastructure includes well-stocked libraries, seminar halls, a large ground, and playfields.

Student Development Programmes: Sports students receive appropriate coaching and are encouraged to participate in state and national-level competitions. Since its inception, the college has earned numerous accolades, with students winning medals, shields, and trophies. NCC cadets consistently distinguish themselves in various events and competitions, while NSS volunteers actively contribute to community and social work. Additionally, the college has several internal clubs and groups that allow like-minded students to connect, broaden their horizons, and enhance their skill sets.
Process to Request Background Verification/Check by Organizations

If any organization wants to conduct background verification/check of a candidate who has studied in any of the campus colleges of Dr. Lankapalli Bullayya College, the following procedure should be followed by the organization or the verification agency:

To confirm from the college (Undergraduate College, Engineering College, Post Graduate College, Junior College) about the genuineness of a candidate who studied here, email the request to bgv@bullayyacollege.org .

To confirm the genuineness of the degree certificate issued to UG, Engineering, PG candidates, please use the portal https://services.andhrauniversity.edu.in of Andhra University, which is the issuing authority of the original degree certificates.
In case of a need to verify the Intermediate Certificate, please request verification from the "Regional Inspection Officer, Board of Intermediate Education, Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh."

Internal Quality Assurance Cell(IQAC)
Co-ordinator (IQAC): Mrs. V. Subbalakshmi, M. Sc., M. Phil.

Since the college was assessed and accredited by the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC), the commitment to quality enhancement initiatives has strengthened significantly. In response, the Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) was established to foster quality awareness and emphasize the importance of quality and its enhancement in both content and delivery among campus functionaries. The IQAC is dedicated to supporting campus functionaries in contributing positively to creating and maintaining the right academic culture and quality standards.
Stakeholder Engagement and Continuous Improvement

Students are our primary stakeholders, and in our mission to deliver high-quality services, the IQAC actively involves teachers in developing better systems and improving processes. To partially fulfil this mission, several measures have been implemented:

1. Student Feedback : Regular feedback from students on functionaries, physical facilities, and services is collected, processed, and shared with relevant parties. Guidance is provided to help improve these areas.

2. Performance Assessment Tools : Tools have been developed to assess the performance levels of functionaries in curricular, co-curricular, and extracurricular areas. Systems are designed to guide improvements and reward improvement.
3. Supportive Systems : Ample scope and freedom are provided within systems and processes to enable functionaries to work efficiently and improve their performance.
4. Periodic Performance Assessments: Peer team assessments are conducted periodically to ensure continuous improvement.
Management Support and Direction

The management's unwavering support for quality enhancement initiatives is instrumental in positioning the college on a progressive trajectory toward quality enhancement in content and delivery for our stakeholders.
About NAAC

The National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) is a national body established by the University Grants Commission (UGC) to assess the practices and performance of higher education institutions in India. NAAC awards grades based on institutional performance, which are indicative of the quality levels of the institutions.
By implementing these measures and continually striving for excellence, the IQAC aims to uphold and advance the academic standards and quality of the college.
